correctness.rationale: Radial homogeneous-degree diagonalization gives the exact Gamma(n+d,1) eigenvalue and degree multiplicity. For alpha<1/2 the Gamma concentration and mean-value bounds yield phase locking; at alpha=1/2 the delta-method Gaussian limit yields exp(-1/8). For alpha>1/2, centered Gamma tails are exponentially small and iterated smooth-cutoff nonstationary integration by parts gives O(k^-M) for every M. Weighted Weyl phase equidistribution proves the circular empirical spectral laws; cluster sets of a normal diagonal operator give the asserted Fredholm essential spectra. Polynomial multiplicities give every Schatten class. The 63 finite checks corroborate but do not replace these arguments.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary text in S. Grudsky and N. Vasilevski (2002), Toeplitz operators on the Fock space: Radial component effects, DOI:10.1007/BF01197858 gives radial diagonalization and compactness of an alpha=1 oscillatory example; K. Esmeral and E. A. Maximenko (2015), arXiv:1505.07906 studies cos|z| at the critical square-root scale. V. Dewage and G. Olafsson (2021), arXiv:2107.01465 provides multidimensional quasi-radial diagonalization. Those are credited as established parts, but no inspected argument gives the full all-alpha spectral phase diagram, the circular complex limiting eigenvalue distributions with multiplicity, or faster-than-polynomial all-Schatten strengthening. The nearest published comparison concerns slow loglog Fock symbols and different operator ideals. Priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Historical priority cannot be guaranteed: earlier radial Toeplitz oscillation theory is substantial; broader compactness results could cover the supercritical compactness subclaim separately.
The literature review covers relevant published primary texts and semantic search but not every mathematical publication; a differently formulated full power-phase theorem could be missed.
The Fulsche 2024 full text comparison is not exhaustive; its general claims do not directly state the specific numerical spectral law.

value.rationale: This class has a natural frequency-versus-Gaussian-width control parameter: derivative of the phase at the Gamma mean times the square-root standard deviation scales as k^(alpha-1/2). Its sharp threshold separates two distinct noncompact circular spectra from an extreme compact regime, despite a nowhere-decaying unimodular symbol. The spectral limiting laws, dimension-independent attenuation at the boundary, and every-Schatten conclusion quantify structural localization and operator-ideal effects beyond the previously known alpha=1 special case.
